recipes.title: Chimichurri Sauce
ingredients:
1 shallot, finely chopped
1 Fresno chile or red jalapeño, finely chopped
3-4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced or finely chopped
1/2 cup red wine vinegar
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or 1/2 tsp. Morton), plus more
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh cilantro (leaves and tender stems)
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley (leaves and tender stems)
2 Tbsp. finely chopped fresh oregano leaves
3/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
steps:
Combine shallot, chile, garlic, vinegar, and salt in a medium bowl. Let sit 10 minutes.
Stir in cilantro, parsley, and oregano.
Whisk in the olive oil.
Transfer 1/2 cup chimichurri to a small bowl; season with salt and reserve as sauce.
Optional marinade: toss remaining chimichurri with beef, chicken, or pork. Cover and chill at least 3 hours or overnight, then grill and spoon reserved chimichurri over the meat.
recipes.servings: About 1½ cups — roughly 8 servings as a sauce (estimated, BA's stated yield wasn't visible)

recipes.title: Ground Venison Jerky
ingredients: 7 lbs venison||1 lb bacon||1 cup dried apples, chopped||16g celery powder||72g salt||2 Tbsp black pepper||1/4 cup onion powder||1/4 cup smoked paprika||2 Tbsp garlic powder||2 tsp ground nutmeg||1 cup water
steps: Grind the venison, bacon, and apples (first on coarse, then on fine).||Mix in the rest of the ingredients.||Cover and refrigerate for 24-48 hours.||Load the jerky gun and press the mixture directly onto dehydrator trays.||Dehydrate at 160°F until dry (roughly 4-5 hours, varies by dehydrator).||Store in the fridge for 3-4 weeks, or freeze for up to 1 year.
recipes.servings: Makes roughly 3-4 lbs finished jerky — about 50 snack-sized servings (rough estimate; yield depends on moisture loss)

recipes.title: Parmesan-Crusted Butter Beans
ingredients: 1 (15-ounce) can butter beans, drained and rinsed||6 ounces Parmesan, freshly grated (about 2 cups)||1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh rosemary||1 tablespoon Calabrian chili paste||Extra-virgin olive oil (about 2 tablespoons, used in the cheese mixture)
steps: Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Line a quarter-sheet pan with parchment paper.||Transfer the butter beans to a cutting board and pat dry.||In a small bowl, combine the Parmesan, rosemary, chili paste, and 2 tablespoons oil; mix to combine.||Scatter the cheese mixture in a thick, even layer across the lined sheet pan. Layer the butter beans on top, making sure none overlap.||Bake until the cheese is golden brown and crisp, 40 to 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool to room temperature.||Carefully slide the beans off the parchment paper, slice into big chunks, and serve.

recipes.title: Spinach Potato Cakes with Cheese
ingredients: 1 large baking potato||1 tbsp olive oil, plus more for frying||4 cups spinach, chopped||2 cloves minced garlic||2 tbsp nutritional yeast||2 tsp garlic powder||1/2 tsp salt||3 tbsp flour||2 tbsp dairy-free butter||1/4 cup dairy-free cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F.||Wrap the potato in foil and bake for 45 minutes, until fully softened.||Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the spinach until wilted.||Peel and mash the potato, then mix thoroughly with the spinach, garlic, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, salt, and flour.||On a floured surface, shape about 1/4 cup of the mixture into a flat circle.||Place about 1 teaspoon of dairy-free butter and 1 tablespoon of dairy-free cheese in the middle, then fold the edges together to form the potato cake shape.||Fry the potato cakes in olive oil for 3-4 minutes, then flip and fry 1-2 minutes more, until crispy.
recipes.servings: About 4 servings (roughly 10-12 potato cakes; estimated, not stated by source)
recipes.imageAlt: Recipe credited to @earthofmariaa within the post; screenshot was shared via @vegan.planvn's repost. Specific post permalink not captured.
